paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God cares about what's TRUE, not what's comfortable. The prophets said what people wanted to hear, and the women with their charms lied to God's people too (Ezekiel 13:19). The prophets said "Peace," when there was no peace (Ezekiel 13:10). Pretty paint on a flimsy wall never made it stand, and a smooth word never made it true.

Why does it matter? Because those lies hurt real people. God says they disheartened the righteous, and they encouraged the wicked not to turn from their evil ways to save their lives (Ezekiel 13:22). A kind-sounding lie can feel like a hug and still leave somebody in the rain. And if the word didn't come from the LORD, then "Thus declares the LORD" is just a costume (Ezekiel 13:6).

So the lesson for you, baker, is to test every word against what God has actually said, and to be careful what you pass along. Ask whether it's truth or just whitewash. And here's the good news that makes me want to dance on my gold base: God steps in for His people. He says, "I will deliver My people from your hands" (Ezekiel 13:23). He won't leave His people trapped under lies, and He's never been fooled by a paint job.
